data.cultural_impact: The name Parama holds a significant cultural impact in Hinduism, as it is commonly used as a name for various deities and religious figures. For instance, Parama Krsna refers to Lord Krishna who is considered the supreme deity, and Parama Shiva refers to Lord Shiva as the ultimate god. In addition, some Hindu philosophies such as Advaita Vedanta emphasize on the ultimate truth or Reality being Paramatma, which is the supreme soul. The name Parama is also used as a title or suffix for spiritual gurus, demonstrating their high spiritual status.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Parama lies in its association with the ultimate reality or consciousness, the paramatma or Param Brahma. In Hinduism, the concept of paramatma refers to the supreme consciousness, the ultimate reality beyond the material world. The name Parama, thus, represents a deep spiritual connection and yearning for the ultimate truth, beyond the transient material life. It evokes a sense of transcendence and a longing for the divine, an aspiration that guides spiritual seekers towards their ultimate goal. Parama is a reminder of the eternal, infinite and pure consciousness that underlies all existence, and the ultimate goal of human life, according to Hindu philosophy.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Parama signifies the supreme or ultimate reality in Hindu philosophy, representing the absolute truth beyond all forms and manifestations, symbolizing the ultimate goal of spiritual pursuit and enlightenment.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
